## {{< fa database >}} Publish a dataset of your own

This page is not part of the pre-work. Nobody sends a dataset before the conference.

In the workshop you see one dataset go from raw files to a data package and its website. If you could imagine publishing a dataset of your own this way, tell me after the workshop, in the room or by email to [{{< var email >}}](mailto:{{< var email >}}), and I follow up with you.

## {{< fa box-open >}} What a published dataset looks like

Each item links to a part of a published example, [guluswm](https://openwashdata.github.io/guluswm/), a household waste survey from Gulu City, Uganda.

-   A [public repository](https://github.com/openwashdata/guluswm) with the processed data, the [code that processed it](https://github.com/openwashdata/guluswm/blob/main/data-raw/data_processing.R) and a [data dictionary](https://github.com/openwashdata/guluswm/blob/main/data-raw/dictionary.csv).
-   A [website for the package](https://openwashdata.github.io/guluswm/) with the documentation of every variable, the data as [CSV and Excel downloads](https://openwashdata.github.io/guluswm/#data) and an [article with plots built from the data](https://openwashdata.github.io/guluswm/articles/examples.html).
-   A [DOI on Zenodo](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23918126) and a [citation](https://openwashdata.github.io/guluswm/authors.html#citation) that names the authors.

## {{< fa shield-halved >}} What the data has to meet

-   It holds no personal data, which means no names, addresses, GPS points of households or other details that identify a person.
-   It may be published under CC BY 4.0 or CC0, because it is yours or because its published licence says so.
